articles.title: NGOs Petition Second Authority to Strip Yitzhak Mirilashvili of Channel 14 or Kol Chai Radio After Legal Exemption Lapses
articles.summary: NGOs 'Lobbby 99' and 'Hatzlacha' filed a petition to Israel's Second Authority arguing that the eight-year legal exemption allowing Yitzhak Mirilashvili to hold both Channel 14 and Kol Chai Radio simultaneously expired in February 2026, demanding enforcement of cross-ownership restrictions.

articles.title: Cross-Ownership Battle Over Channel 14 and Kol Chai Leads Today's Israeli Press Front Pages
articles.updateOf: NGOs Petition Second Authority to Strip Yitzhak Mirilashvili of Channel 14 or Kol Chai Radio After Legal Exemption Lapses
articles.summary: The 7th Eye's Aug 10 press-digest highlights the Mirilashvili cross-ownership challenge as the lead media story of the day, signaling continued editorial and regulatory momentum against his simultaneous control of the TV channel and the Haredi radio station.

articles.title: Legal Exemption Expired: How Will the Second Authority Act Against Mirilashvili's Dual Media Holdings?
articles.summary: Deep-dive analysis noting that the statutory cross-ownership ban on simultaneous TV and radio ownership was reactivated in February 2026 and that Yitzhak Mirilashvili, who also holds 100% of Kol Chai after buying out minority partners in 2025, has yet to divest either asset.

articles.title: Seizing Oligarch Yachts Sounded Great. Then Taxpayers Got the Bill.
articles.updateOf: Amadea Finally Sold After Years of Legal Battles — Disputes Still Live
articles.summary: Forbes investigative feature reveals the Amadea's four-year US custody cost taxpayers an estimated $36M in maintenance, with the government netting only ~$150M after costs from the $187M sale — and none of the proceeds earmarked for Ukraine.

articles.title: Georgescu Uses Mihai Viteazul Anniversary to Attack 'Anti-Christian Globalists' in Political Facebook Post
articles.summary: Despite facing trial, Georgescu published a charged political message on August 9 drawing a parallel between the 1601 assassination of Mihai Viteazul and today's 'anti-Christian globalists,' signalling continued far-right political activity.

articles.title: Bucharest Court of Appeal Now Empowered to Schedule First Substantive Hearing in Georgescu-Potra Coup Case
articles.updateOf: Romania's Supreme Court Greenlights Full Coup-Attempt Trial Against Georgescu and Mercenary Leader Potra
articles.summary: Following the ICCJ's August 6 final ruling, the Bucharest Court of Appeal is now formally authorised to set the date for the first on-the-merits hearing in the 22-defendant coup case, marking the next concrete procedural step.

articles.title: House Russia-Iran Sanctions Vote Pushed to September as Congress Enters Recess
articles.updateOf: Senate Passes Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 86-11, Heads to House
articles.summary: A House floor vote on the Graham Russia-Iran sanctions bill — which Ortagus publicly championed — will not occur until at least early September, as the lower chamber has entered its five-week August recess, leaving the bill's fate uncertain amid Democratic resistance over tariff provisions.

articles.title: Musk/Spiro File Ninth Circuit Appeal of Twitter Fraud Verdict and Post-Trial Rulings
articles.updateOf: Judge Breyer Denies Musk/Spiro Post-Trial Motions to Void Twitter Fraud Verdict
articles.summary: Musk, represented by Spiro, filed a formal notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit challenging the orders that largely upheld the March fraud verdict, with estimated damages of up to $2.6 billion.

articles.title: Alex Spiro Joins MasTec Board of Directors as Class III Director
articles.summary: NYSE-listed infrastructure giant MasTec appointed Spiro as a Class III director and Compensation Committee member, citing his decade of advising Fortune 500 companies on regulatory, securities, and litigation matters.

articles.title: Channel 14 Re-Files Contempt Petition Against Democrats Party Over Repeated Press Exclusion
articles.summary: Channel 14 filed a new administrative petition at Tel Aviv District Court (עת"מ 6501-08-26) alleging the Democrats party violated the Supreme Court's 2022 press-access precedent by again barring its crews from a party primary event, seeking a declaratory order compelling equal access to all party events.

articles.title: Government Advertising Spend on Channel 14 Sets New Record: NIS 7.1M in 2025, Up 368% Since 2022
articles.summary: Newly disclosed official data show the Netanyahu government paid a record NIS 7.1 million in state advertising to Yitzhak Mirilashvili's Channel 14 in 2025 — a 9% rise on the previous record year and a 368% surge versus 2022, intensifying scrutiny of the channel's regulatory treatment.

articles.title: Israeli Press Front Pages (11.8.2026): Mirilashvili Cross-Ownership Issue Leads Third Consecutive Day
articles.updateOf: Cross-Ownership Battle Over Channel 14 and Kol Chai Leads Today's Israeli Press Front Pages
articles.summary: Today's Israeli press digest confirms Mirilashvili's dual ownership of Channel 14 and Kol Chai radio — and the Second Authority's pending response — remains the dominant Israeli media story for a third consecutive day, with no regulatory decision announced yet.

articles.title: Kazakhstan Weighs New Oil Export Routes as Drone Strikes Squeeze Black Sea Shipments
articles.updateOf: Tankers Resume Oil Loadings at Key Kazakh CPC Export Terminal After Attacks
articles.summary: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry is actively evaluating the BTC pipeline, Baku-Supsa route, and trans-Caspian Azerbaijan transit as emergency alternatives after Ukrainian drone strikes suspended CPC Black Sea loadings three times in July alone, halving national oil output at its peak.

articles.title: California Federal Court Denies CREXi Stay Bid in CoStar Copyright Case Amid Quinn Emanuel DQ Appeal
articles.updateOf: CREXi Petitions Ninth Circuit to Undo Quinn Emanuel/Spiro Disqualification in CoStar Copyright Fight
articles.summary: A California federal judge rejected CREXi's bid to stay the CoStar copyright suit while CREXi pursues its Ninth Circuit appeal of Quinn Emanuel's disqualification, forcing CREXi to proceed without Spiro's team.

articles.title: Second Authority Regulator's Representative Concealed Post-Appointment Meetings with Communications Minister Kara'i
articles.updateOf: Legal Exemption Expired: How Will the Second Authority Act Against Mirilashvili's Dual Media Holdings?
articles.summary: A freedom-of-information request reveals that Yoni Shemoni — Communications Minister Kara'i's appointee on the Second Authority council, the body that must rule on Mirilashvili's illegal cross-ownership — held two meetings with Kara'i after his appointment while publicly denying any contact, raising serious conflict-of-interest questions about the regulator's independence.

articles.title: Israeli Press Front Pages (12.8.2026): Mirilashvili Cross-Ownership Issue Leads Fourth Consecutive Day
articles.updateOf: Israeli Press Front Pages (11.8.2026): Mirilashvili Cross-Ownership Issue Leads Third Consecutive Day
articles.summary: The 12 August 2026 daily press-front-page roundup again leads with the lapsed exemption permitting Yitzhak Mirilashvili to hold Channel 14 and Kol Chai simultaneously, marking a fourth consecutive day the story dominates Israeli newspaper front pages with no Second Authority decision yet announced.

articles.title: Newsweek Publishes Opinion Calling on US to Defend Democracy and Georgescu in Romania
articles.summary: A Newsweek opinion piece by London-based writer Dennis Portman argues the US should publicly defend the democratic rights of the nine million Romanians who voted in 2024 and challenge Romania's election annulment process, framing it as a NATO security concern.

articles.title: The Diplomatic Affairs: Newsweek Entry Into Romanian Debate Signals Growing Western Attention to Georgescu Case
articles.summary: Analysis piece notes that Newsweek's August 11 editorial calling on Washington to defend Georgescu's voters marks a significant escalation of Western media attention to Romania's election annulment controversy.

articles.title: Coup-Plot File Formally Returns to Bucharest Court of Appeal for Merits Hearing Scheduling
articles.updateOf: Bucharest Court of Appeal Now Empowered to Schedule First Substantive Hearing in Georgescu-Potra Coup Case
articles.summary: Following the ICCJ's Aug 6 definitive ruling, the Georgescu-Potra coup-attempt dossier has formally been returned to the Bucharest Court of Appeal, which will now set concrete hearing dates and begin administering evidence.

articles.title: House Bipartisan Group Introduces Graham Sanctions Companion Bill During Recess, Teeing Up Fall Vote
articles.updateOf: House Russia-Iran Sanctions Vote Pushed to September as Congress Enters Recess
articles.summary: Despite the House remaining in August recess, Reps. McCaul, Fitzpatrick, Hoyer and 16 colleagues introduced an identical companion to the Senate-passed Graham sanctions bill on Aug. 10, accelerating momentum toward a fall floor vote and complicating the earlier framing that action was simply deferred to September.

articles.title: Trump's Iran Tariff Demand Looms as Key Obstacle for Graham Sanctions Bill in the House
articles.summary: House aides warn that Trump's standing demand to add Iran tariff authority to the Graham Act — which Democrats already oppose — is the central fault line that could prevent passage under suspension rules requiring a two-thirds majority.

articles.title: SC Senate Special Primary Forces Aug. 25 Runoff Between Darline Graham and Ralph Norman
articles.summary: No candidate cleared a majority in last night's South Carolina GOP special primary to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, sending Trump-endorsed appointed Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman to an Aug. 25 runoff — leaving uncertain who will champion the Graham sanctions act's Senate legacy in the new term.

articles.title: Israeli Press Front Pages (13.8.2026): Mirilashvili Cross-Ownership Issue Leads Fifth Consecutive Day
articles.updateOf: Israeli Press Front Pages (12.8.2026): Mirilashvili Cross-Ownership Issue Leads Fourth Consecutive Day
articles.summary: The Seventh Eye's daily press-digest confirms the Mirilashvili dual-ownership story headlines Israeli papers for a fifth straight day, alongside the ongoing story of the Second Authority representative concealing meetings with Minister Karhi.

articles.title: Second Authority Grants Channel 14 New Reprieve on Jerusalem Broadcast Requirement Until End of August
articles.summary: The Second Authority council deferred enforcement of Channel 14's legal obligation to broadcast news from Jerusalem, granting a further reprieve until either Minister Karhi's communications law takes effect or end of August 2026 — whichever comes first — even though the channel's exemption period expired in February 2026.
